title: Smooth-stratum finite-Tor devissage over an arbitrary algebraically closed field
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field, $A$ a finite commutative ring, and $X$ a separated finite-type $F$-scheme. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on small etale sites and their derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let $a\leq b$ be integers and let $K\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ be bounded constructible [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] with Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, meaning that $\mathcal H^q(K\otimes_A^LM)=0$ for every module sheaf $M$ in degree zero and every $q\notin[a,b]$ [def-kun-derived-tensor, def-kun-tor-amplitude].

There is a finite partition of the underlying space of $X$ into reduced (with no nonzero nilpotents in their local rings), smooth, connected (not a union of two disjoint nonempty open subsets) locally closed $F$-subschemes $s_r:S_r\hookrightarrow X$, each of pure dimension $e_r\leq\dim X$, meaning that every irreducible component has dimension $e_r$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], with the following properties. Put $P_r=s_r^{-1}K$ using exact constant-coefficient inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Each $P_r$ has finite locally constant cohomology. There is an etale cover of $S_r$ on which $P_r$ is represented by a complex of constant finite projective $A$-modules zero outside $[a,b]$; a finite projective $A$-module here means a direct summand of a finite free $A$-module.

Moreover there are objects $F_0=K,F_1,\ldots,F_m=0$ and distinguished triangles
$$Rs_{r!}P_r\longrightarrow F_{r-1}\longrightarrow F_r\longrightarrow Rs_{r!}P_r[1]\qquad(1\leq r\leq m).$$
Here $Rs_{r!}=j_!i_*$ for a factorization $S_r\xrightarrow{i}V\xrightarrow{j}X$ with $i$ closed and $j$ open; the closed direct image is exact, and $j_!$ is ordinary etale extension by zero [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement, def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. The triangles are in the ordinary etale derived category [def-weil-triangulated-category]. No restriction of $F$ to an algebraic closure of a finite field is imposed.
